description:
EF 3.1 ships `cerium(3+)` on thirteen emission rows and writes 7440-45-1 on every one -- the registry number of cerium the element, which EF also publishes, under the same number, as its `cerium` resource row. A stated number outranks a name, so on the 2026-08-29 build of `54b0f9d` the thirteen rows joined the resource row on one substance published as `Cerium`, and the charge EF wrote on purpose was dropped. EF's other dissolved metals -- `iron (iii)`, `chromium (vi)`, `vanadium (v)` -- keep their charge; cerium was the one whose number contradicted its name.

The decision the issue asked for: the name is believed, as it was for `vanadium (v)` (#49) and for BAFU's five `X II` rows (#146). `ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json` writes the ion's own number, 18923-26-7 (PubChem CID 114853; ChEBI:48782), on the thirteen rows. The element keeps its resource row and BAFU's `Cerium` in river water, which BAFU registers as the element.

Measured on the build of 2026-08-29 at `54b0f9d`: one substance carries 7440-45-1 with fifteen flows, and no substance carries 18923-26-7. See #184.

expectations.title: A substance registered as cerium(3+) exists and holds EF's thirteen emission flows
expectations.comment: The positive half. Thirteen flows, one per EF emission context, and no more: nothing on any merged list carries the ion's number or the ion's name, so no source row joins them.

expectations.title: EF's cerium(3+) in urban air is published under the ion's number
expectations.comment: One of the thirteen the issue names, on its own so the count above cannot hold while a flow slips back to the element. `characterised` because these are the rows that carry EF's toxicity factors for the ion, and the point of separating them is that those numbers stop being published as the element's.

expectations.title: Cerium the element keeps its resource row and BAFU's river row, and nothing else
expectations.comment: The leave-alone half. Before: fifteen flows, thirteen of them the ion's. After: EF's `cerium` resource row and BAFU's `Cerium` to river water, which BAFU registers 7440-45-1 and which stays where its number puts it.
